findings.problem: Clean Code E1. Counting code points of trimmed text is written three ways in this diff: `lengthOf` here (spread), `charCount` in reference-proof.ts (`Array.from(text.trim()).length`) and `truncateTaskText` in context-resolver.ts (`Array.from(text)`). The two helpers have identical behaviour and different names.
findings.impact: Two names for one concept; a future fix to the counting rule (for example graphemes instead of code points) has to be applied in each place.
findings.suggested_fix: One exported `codePointLength(text)` in a small shared module, used by both helpers.
findings.evidence: reference-proof.ts: `return Array.from(text.trim()).length;` inside `charCount`.

findings.problem:
A UTF-8 BOM at the start of a markdown document sits before the first '#', so the first-line heading is not recognised. The BOM is stripped for references.json (loadReferences) but not for the documents read by extractSection / readDeclaredFile / inspectDocument. Verified: extractSection('﻿# Title
text
## B
x
', 'Title') returns found:false with available ['B'].
findings.impact: Trigger: a declared document saved with a BOM whose anchor is its first-line H1. The resolver warns 'anchor not found' and falls back to the whole file; `check` reports anchor-not-found as an error while the heading is visible in any editor. Cost is a confusing diagnostic, and with F-001 an unsatisfiable proof.
findings.suggested_fix: In scanHeadings, strip a leading U+FEFF from the first line before matching (keeping offsets consistent with markdown.slice, i.e. treat the BOM as part of the section prefix).
findings.evidence: Ran extractSection at head with the BOM input: {"found":false,"anchor":"Title","reason":"no heading matches anchor \"Title\"","available":["B"]}.

findings.problem: references-section.test.ts pins backtick fences only with a plain opener and closer. The fence-closing conditions (tilde fences, a closing run shorter than the opening one, a different marker, a closing line with trailing text) and a heading made only of closing hashes have no case.
findings.impact: A fence that is closed too early or too late would change which headings count, and so the section bytes that become the budget and the obligation. Mutating the comparison from >= to > or dropping the marker equality would pass the suite.
findings.suggested_fix: Add cases: a ~~~ fence containing a '# not a heading' line; a four-backtick opener that a three-backtick line does not close; a backtick fence not closed by ~~~; a heading line '## ##'.
findings.evidence: Read src/gdskills/references-section.test.ts in the slice (lines 1315-1467): one fenced case only.

findings.problem: Clean Code A1/B3. The `flags` array literal in `renderResolutionMarkdown` is now one line of several hundred characters, and the new element puts a template literal with a nested conditional template inside an array element that already holds three ternaries. The reader has to parse four conditional levels to see what is rendered.
findings.impact: Hard to review or extend; the next flag has to be appended into the same line.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract `entryFlags(entry): string[]` with one statement per flag, and `anchorFlag(entry)` for the anchor and section size.
findings.evidence: Diff hunk '@@ 1,62 @@' of resolve-context-command.ts, the `const flags = [...]` line.

findings.problem: A ternary nested inside a template literal that is itself the branch of a ternary, packed on one line into an array of four other ternaries (the `flags` array is now one line of several hundred characters).
findings.impact: Hard to read and to review; adding the next flag means editing a line that is already past what the eye can parse.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract a small `anchorFlag(entry)` helper returning the string or "", and put the flags array one element per line.
findings.evidence: Single added line in renderResolutionMarkdown.

findings.problem: docFixture fills the ContextEntry `bytes` field (and budget `usedBytes`) with `text.length`, a character count. The same slice's context-resolver tests use Buffer.byteLength for the same field, and the Russian-section test in this file passes Cyrillic text through docFixture, so the fixture's `bytes` is not a byte count there.
findings.impact: The field name says bytes and the project cares about the bytes/characters difference (references-section.test.ts asserts it). A reader copying this fixture gets a wrong value for non-ASCII text; a future check on `bytes` would pass or fail for the wrong reason.
findings.suggested_fix: Use Buffer.byteLength(text, "utf8") for `bytes` and `usedBytes` in docFixture.
findings.evidence: In the diff of src/gdskills/resolved-context-check.test.ts, docFixture sets `bytes: text.length` and `usedBytes: text.length`; the test 'summary: letters of any script count...' calls docFixture({ text: "## Токены..." }).

findings.quote: const report = await checkResolvedContext({ projectRoot: root, resolved, result: cite(sha) });
findings.problem: The new block repeats `await checkResolvedContext({ projectRoot: root, resolved, result: ... })` more than twenty times, many of them wrapped over five lines, only to read `.misses` or `.drifted`. docFixture already returns `{ root, resolved, sha }`, so a local `check(fixture, extra)` helper fits.
findings.impact: The meaning of each test (what is cited, which rule is expected) is buried in call plumbing, and a change to the checker's input shape touches every test.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a small helper, for example `const rulesOf = async (f, extra) => (await checkResolvedContext({ projectRoot: f.root, resolved: f.resolved, result: cite(f.sha, extra) })).misses.map((m) => m.rule)`, and assert on its result.
findings.evidence: The hunks 'summary: a missing or different anchor...', 'summary: fewer than 40 characters...', 'summary: exactly two shared words...' and 'summary: letters of any script count...' all repeat the same call shape.

findings.quote: Flow 461 semantics: the last citation of each path is the one that counts for the hash.
findings.problem: The question 'which citation of this path counts' is answered by two unrelated rules in two modules: the hash check takes the last citation (`cited.get(where)?.at(-1)`), while the proof takes pickProofItem, which prefers a citation with the pinned sha256 and a real reading and otherwise falls back to the first non-n/a item. appliedOf now keeps every citation of a path, which makes the two rules able to pick different items.
findings.impact: Trigger: project_context_applied lists a promoted path twice. If the last item carries the pinned sha256 with how n/a and an earlier item carries a different sha256 with how read, a good anchor and a good summary, the hash check passes on the last item and the proof passes on the earlier one, so no miss is emitted for an entry that was last cited with n/a and with a hash that did not match on the item that proved it. AC11 (promoted entry cited with n/a is a miss) is met only for the single-citation case.
findings.suggested_fix: Select one citation per path once, in appliedOf or in checkResolvedContext, and feed the same item to the hash check and to proofFailures; or require that the proof item also carries the pinned sha256.
findings.evidence: Diff: `const last = cited.get(where)?.at(-1);` feeds `shas`; `pickProofItem(items, entry.sha256)` in proofMisses is `items.find((item) => item.sha256 === pinned && item.how !== "n/a") ?? items.find((item) => item.how !== "n/a") ?? items[0]`. With items [A{sha: other, how: read}, B{sha: pinned, how: n/a}] the first find returns undefined, the second returns A, and B satisfies `shas.includes(entry.sha256)`.

findings.problem: This test (the AC17 pin for the instruction edits in this slice) asks only that each of the five instruction files contains `--task-text` once. job-orchestrator/SKILL.md carries the flag at two resolve sites in the diff (Step A and the fix loop) and orchestrator-prompt.md at two (the test resolve and the fix step); removing it from the fix-loop line leaves the file matching through the other site. The same holds for the per-file 'promoted entry needs path, sha256, anchor and a summary' paragraph test, which is satisfied by any single paragraph.
findings.impact: The fix dispatch is the case that re-resolves on a new head; if its line loses `--task-text`, a keyword-only document silently stops promoting on the fix attempt while AC17's test stays green. The test file itself is outside the slice diff; the lines it guards are in it.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert per site rather than per file: count the `keryx skills resolve-context` occurrences that carry a `--out` and require `--task-text` on each, or snapshot the specific lines the diff touched.
findings.evidence: Read skill-sync.test.ts lines 40-52 and the diff hunks for job-orchestrator SKILL.md (resolve-context at Step A and fix step 3) and orchestrator-prompt.md (step 1 and FIX step 2). Reasoned, not run. mutant candidates m11, m12 below.

findings.problem: The adapter that turns the port call into the resolver call forwards taskText, but src/harness/tool/metaproject-adapter.test.ts has no skillsResolveContext test and the slice adds none. Removing the spread keeps every test green.
findings.impact: The harness tool path could lose task_text between the op layer and the resolver while the op-layer test stays green, so keyword promotion would silently stop working for harness agents.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an adapter test over a tmp project that has a references.json with a keyword condition: call skillsResolveContext with taskText containing the keyword and assert the entry is must_read with reason condition:keyword:<k>; call it without taskText and assert on_demand.
findings.evidence: Read src/harness/tool/metaproject-adapter.test.ts in full: no skillsResolveContext case. Slice hunk for metaproject-adapter.ts is production-only.

findings.problem: `--task-text <text>` goes through optionValue, which treats any following token that starts with `--` as the next flag and returns undefined. A task title or description that begins with `--` (a CLI flag as the topic, or a markdown `-- ` aside) is therefore dropped without a word: resolve-context-command treats it as no task text, records none, and warns about nothing.
findings.impact: Trigger: `keryx skills resolve-context ... --task-text "--no-cache build flag"`. Outcome: keyword-declared references are not promoted, the worker is not obliged to read them, and nothing says why. The only visible sign is the missing promotion, so the gate fails open. Narrow: it needs a text starting with `--`, and the `--task-text=<text>` spelling is unaffected.
findings.suggested_fix: In runResolveContextCommand, read `--task-text` with a parser that accepts a leading `--` (for example take args[index + 1] verbatim for this option), or fail loudly with 'use --task-text=<text>' when the flag is present with no usable value. Add a test for a text starting with `--`.
findings.evidence: src/lib/args.ts lines 18-28 (the guard on line 24); resolve-context-command.ts line 40 `const taskText = optionValue(args, "--task-text");` followed by the `taskText !== undefined && taskText.trim() !== ""` guards; no warning is emitted for the dropped text.

findings.problem: The MCP structured branch for skills_resolve_context forwards task_text to the port on its own code path (it returns port.skillsResolveContext directly and never calls op.invoke). No test exercises task_text on that path: src/mcp/metaproject-tools.test.ts calls the tool only with { files, for }, and src/harness/tool/metaproject-operations.test.ts (new test 'passes task_text to the port as taskText') covers op.invoke, which this branch bypasses. The adapter line that forwards input.taskText to resolveProjectContext in metaproject-adapter.ts is also untested (no skillsResolveContext match in metaproject-adapter.test.ts).
findings.impact: AC3 names the MCP call as a carrier of the task text. Dropping the taskText spread in either place would silently disable keyword promotion for every MCP caller (all keyword-only declarations stay on_demand) and no test would fail.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one case to src/mcp/metaproject-tools.test.ts: write a references.json with a keyword declaration, invoke skills_resolve_context with task_text containing the keyword, and assert the entry is must_read with reason condition:keyword:<kw>; the same call without task_text stays on_demand.
findings.evidence: keryx ctx rg for skills_resolve_context in src/mcp tests shows only the files/for call at metaproject-tools.test.ts:56 and :111-:140; ripgrep for skillsResolveContext in metaproject-adapter.test.ts returns no match; the slice diff for metaproject-tools.ts adds the taskText lines only inside the bespoke case that returns port.skillsResolveContext(...) directly.

findings.problem: The two new type imports from ../gdskills/ are inserted after the `./modal-host` import, inside the sibling-import group, and `references-config` precedes `references-check`. The file's existing order is ../gdskills/* first, then ./* siblings.
findings.impact: Breaks the group-then-alphabetical ordering the rest of the file follows, so the next import added has no obvious place. ESLint config does not enforce import order, so nothing else will catch it.
findings.suggested_fix: Move both imports up beside the other ../gdskills/ type imports, ordered references-check before references-config.
findings.evidence: Diff hunk at the top of src/tui/project-context-inspector.test.ts: after `import type { OpenModalInput } from "./modal-host";` come the two `../gdskills/references-*` imports.

findings.problem: The R4 fixture sets exceeded: true with usedBytes: 109 against limitBytes: 131072, a state the resolver can never produce (exceeded means usedBytes is over limitBytes). The test then asserts the sentence 'over the cap: 109 of 131072 bytes', which is false for those numbers.
findings.impact: The test pins the wording of an impossible record, so it will not catch a presenter bug that prints the wrong pair of numbers, and it documents misleading output for a future reader.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the over-cap record with usedBytes greater than limitBytes (for example limitBytes 100, usedBytes 109) and assert 'over the cap: 109 of 100 bytes'.
findings.evidence: Fixture line in the slice: budget: { limitBytes: 131072, usedBytes: 109, exceeded, limitSource: "default" }, with section_bytes 120.

findings.problem: The R7 test pushes a feed update after close and then asserts the Status text. The Status text is the same for the 'before' and 'after' snapshots, so the assertion passes whether or not the closed inspector kept repainting.
findings.impact: A regression that repaints or re-subscribes after close (the 'closed ||' guards in the presenter) would not be caught; it would leak listeners and render into a disposed node.
findings.suggested_fix: Push a record that changes visible text (for example a different budget) after close and assert the text is unchanged, or compare node identity from h.node() before and after the post-close push, and assert the feed has zero subscribers after close.
findings.evidence: Test flow: push?.(before) is followed by a post-close push and the Status assertion above; both snapshots render identical Status text.

findings.problem: Adding the References tab extended a tab-id-to-formatter mapping that is spelled out separately in four places: the nested three-way ternary in paint(), the Math.max(...) list that sizes contentRows, the tabs array, and the ProjectContextTab union. Meanwhile `let tab: string` (was the untyped `let tab = "status"`) ignores the newly added ProjectContextTab type, and ProjectContextCommand declares its own inline `tab?: "references"` literal. A fourth tab means editing all of these in step, and a miss (a tab missing from the contentRows max) silently mis-sizes the modal rather than failing a type check.
findings.impact: Maintenance cost on the next tab addition (OCP smell); no wrong behaviour today.
findings.suggested_fix: Hold one table keyed by ProjectContextTab, e.g. `const TAB_LINES: Record<ProjectContextTab, (s: ProjectContextStatus) => string[]>`, and derive paint(), the contentRows maximum and the tabs list from it; type `tab` as ProjectContextTab and have ProjectContextCommand reuse `Extract<ProjectContextTab, "references">`.
findings.evidence: Diff hunk @@ 76,283 of project-context-inspector.ts: paint() ternary, contentRows `Math.max(formatProjectContextStatusLines(status).length, formatProjectContextLastLines(status).length, formatProjectReferencesLines(status).length) + 2`, `let tab: string = options.initialTab ?? "status"`; ProjectContextTab is declared at line ~21 and used only for `initialTab?: ProjectContextTab`.

findings.problem: reload() runs subscriber callbacks inside the same async function as the load, and poll() catches everything and reports it as a failed poll. A throwing subscriber (the sidebar repaint touches renderer objects) therefore (a) skips the remaining listeners, including an open modal's repaint, because `current` is already advanced and the next poll sees no change, and (b) is surfaced to the operator as a load failure ('projectctx: <message>') with `failing` set. Load errors and listener errors are one catch.
findings.impact: Only reachable if a subscriber throws (for example a repaint against a destroyed renderable); the symptom would be an open References tab that stops updating until the status changes again, with a misleading error. Not shown to occur in the diff, so kept at minor.
findings.suggested_fix: Isolate listeners: wrap each `listener(next)` in its own try/catch that reports through options.onError (or let guardedThemeRepaint-style guards own it), so one failing subscriber neither starves the others nor masquerades as a failed poll.
findings.evidence: Diff: createProjectContextFeed reload()/poll(); refreshProjectContextSidebar (tui-shell.ts) is subscribed via `projectContextFeed.subscribe(refreshProjectContextSidebar)` and clears/re-adds renderables; the modal listener calls paint().

findings.problem: The project-context feed polls with setInterval and an async tick (poll -> reload -> options.load) with no in-flight guard. A tick starts every 5000 ms whether or not the previous load has finished. reload() also assigns `current` and notifies listeners in completion order, not start order. Implementation sits outside the slice diff; the slice's `R7 the feed reloads on an interval...` test covers it and never exercises overlapping or out-of-order loads.
findings.impact: Trigger: load takes longer than 5 s (slow or network disk, large rules tree, the references check reading many files). Overlapping loads then pile up, one extra file scan per tick. A slower, older load can finish last and overwrite a newer status, so the sidebar and open modal show a stale resolve until the next change. Bounded by one TUI session, hence minor.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a single in-flight flag or reuse the pending promise in poll()/reload() (skip the tick while one is running), and drop a result whose start sequence number is older than the last applied. Add a test with a load that resolves after the next tick.
findings.evidence: src/tui/project-context-inspector.ts lines 149-155 (defaultInterval) and 167-186 (reload/poll/stop wiring); the test at `R7 the feed reloads on an interval and tells listeners only when the status changed` drives tick() sequentially with immediately-resolving loads only.

findings.problem: This flow adds `export type ProjectContextTab = "status" | "last" | "references"` and uses it for `initialTab`, but the working variable `tab` is widened to `string`, and the literal `"references"` is repeated as the separate single-member type `tab?: "references"` in the `open` command variant and in `showProjectContext(tab?: "references")` in tui-shell.ts. The tab ids are therefore spelled in four places that the compiler does not tie together; the tab list in `openModalFn` repeats them again as strings.
findings.impact: Renaming or adding a tab id compiles cleanly and leaves one of the sites silently stale (for example a `paint` branch that never matches). Convention-consistency cost only; no wrong behaviour today.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare `let tab: ProjectContextTab = options.initialTab ?? "status";`, narrow the `renderTab` argument with a guard or cast once, and type the command and shell parameter as `Extract<ProjectContextTab, "references">` (or a named `ProjectContextOpenTab`) so one type owns the ids.
findings.evidence: Slice diff: `export type ProjectContextTab` (line 23 of the hunk), `let tab: string = ...`, `{ kind: "open"; /** Absent: the Status tab. */ tab?: "references" }`, and `const showProjectContext = (tab?: "references"): void` in tui-shell.ts.

findings.problem: `formatProjectReferencesLines` is imported a few lines above for use in this file and then re-exported from the same module. Production code imports neither symbol from the inspector (tui-shell.ts does not); only project-context-inspector.test.ts reads them through it, while both are defined and exported by project-references-view.ts.
findings.impact: Unnecessary indirection: two import paths for one symbol, and the inspector looks like the owner of text that lives in project-references-view.ts. Small maintenance cost.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the re-export and have the test import `NO_REFERENCES_TEXT` and `formatProjectReferencesLines` from `./project-references-view`.
findings.evidence: keryx ctx rg for NO_REFERENCES_TEXT|formatProjectReferencesLines|createProjectContextFeed over src and docs: consumers outside the view file are project-context-inspector.test.ts and the inspector itself; tui-shell.ts imports only createProjectContextFeed among the new names.

findings.quote: return status.last?.result.entries.find((entry) => entry.path === declaration.path && entry.condition !== undefined);
findings.problem: The 'R2 only declared entries count' test cites OTHER.md, which is not a declared path, so the entry.path === declaration.path half of the predicate excludes it and the entry.condition !== undefined half is never decisive. Removing the condition clause keeps the test green.
findings.impact: A cited contract at a declared path, with no condition, would be shown as a promoted or resolved reference of the declaration. The R2 count would then include documents the rules cited rather than the conditions promoted.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a resolved entry for a declared path with no condition field (a rule-cited contract) and assert the declaration stays unresolved (R2 count excludes it).
findings.evidence: Fixture line: const cited: RefEntry = { kind: "contract", source: "project", path: "OTHER.md", sha256: "q", bytes: 5, reason: "cited by AGENTS.mdc", tier: "must_read" };

findings.problem: createProjectContextFeed starts a 5 s setInterval at construction and returns stop(), but the shell never calls projectContextFeed.stop(). Every other live panel/poller in this shell is released in the renderer's onDestroy (disposeExecutionPlanPanel, liveSchedules.dispose(), liveIntake.dispose(), liveDecisions.dispose() and others). After the renderer is destroyed the poll keeps running and, when the status changes, calls the subscribed refreshProjectContextSidebar, which does clearTranscriptChildren/sbProjectCtx.add on destroyed renderables.
findings.impact: Lifecycle ownership is inconsistent with the siblings. The timer is unref'd, so it does not hold the process open, and a throwing listener is caught by poll() and reported through onError, so the observable harm is a leaked timer plus a possible stray 'projectctx: ...' system line after teardown, mainly where a shell is torn down inside a longer-lived process (tests, embedding). Verified: `keryx ctx rg projectContextFeed src/tui/tui-shell.ts` returns 5 matches, none is .stop().
findings.suggested_fix: Call projectContextFeed.stop() in the createShellRenderer onDestroy block next to the other dispose() calls (the feed is declared later in the same scope, so hoist a `let stopProjectContextFeed: (() => void) | undefined` as disposeExecutionPlanPanel is, or register it where liveSchedules is). Optionally make the listener a no-op once destroyed.
findings.evidence: src/tui/tui-shell.ts onDestroy block (disposeExecutionPlanPanel?.(); liveSchedules?.dispose(); ...) has no feed stop; slice-05 hunk @@ 5249 creates the feed with the default interval; defaultInterval returns () => clearInterval(timer) as stop.
